statement.p: Find the point on the graph of z=y^{2}-2x^{2} at which vector \mathbf{n}=\left\lt -12,8,-1 \right> is normal to the tangent plane.

static.solution:
(a, b, f(a,b)) on the graph z=f(x,y) is z=f(a,b)+f_x(a,b)(x-a)+f_y(a,b)(y-b) or f_x(a,b)(x-a)+f_y(a,b)(y-b)-z+f(a,b)=0 Therefore the following vector is normal to the plane: \mathbf{v}=\left\lt f_x(a,b), f_y(a,b), -1\right> We compute the partial derivatives of the function f(x,y)=y^{2}-2x^{2}:
\left. \begin{array}{lcl} f_x(x,y)=-4x \amp \Rightarrow \amp f_x(a,b)=-4a \\ f_y(x,y)=2y \amp \Rightarrow \amp f_y(a,b)=2b \end{array} \right.
Therefore, the vector \mathbf{v}=\left\lt -4a, 2b, -1\right> is normal to the tangent plane at (a,b).
Since we want \mathbf{n}=\left\lt -12,8,-1 \right> to be normal to the plane, the vectors \mathbf{v} and \mathbf{n} must be parallel.
That is, the following must hold:
\frac{-4a}{-12}=\frac{2b}{8}=\frac{-1}{-1} which implies that a=3 and b=4. We compute the z-coordinate of the point: z=b^{2}-2a^{2}=-2
